dossier.summary: Ridgeview Dental Group runs eleven dental offices in two states with one shared front desk team.

chapters.title: Welcome and what we measured
chapters.summary: Elena Ruiz and Jonas Berg introduce a study of appointment no-shows across 60 practices.

chapters.title: Why more reminders stop working
chapters.summary: Past the third reminder, extra messages brought no appointments back. Patients who ignore two texts rarely answer a third.

chapters.title: Confirm or cancel beats a plain reminder
chapters.summary: A reply to confirm or cancel cut no-shows more than a plain reminder, because cancelled slots could be rebooked.

chapters.title: Filling cancelled slots the same day
chapters.summary: Practices with a same-day waitlist refilled about a third of the slots that were cancelled.

chapters.title: Running it with a small front desk
chapters.summary: How a front desk of two to four people handles replies and the waitlist without a new hire.

chapters.title: Questions: insurance checks, multi-office scheduling
chapters.summary: Questions on insurance checks, patients without a cell phone and scheduling across several offices.

chapters.title: Close and the practice checklist
chapters.summary: Wrap up and where to get the checklist.

slide_pages.caption: No-show rate by number of reminders
A same-day waitlist, step by step

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: The change that surprised us was small. We stopped saying "reminder" and asked patients to confirm or cancel. A cancel is a good outcome for a practice, because the slot is still open for two days.

transcript.speaker: Jonas
transcript.text: And the front desk does not chase anyone. A patient who does not answer is treated as unconfirmed and moves to the list for a phone call, which is a short list.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Right. Fewer messages go out in total, but each one asks for something the patient can do in ten seconds.

data.book_title: Want to see it with your offices' numbers?
data.book_text: Jonas can go through the no-show study with your front desk lead in 20 minutes and show where your offices would start.

takeaways.title: Ask patients to confirm or cancel
takeaways.body: A confirm or cancel reply cut no-shows more than a plain reminder did. Cancelled slots could be rebooked, which helps a group that runs many schedules.

takeaways.title: Keep a same-day waitlist
takeaways.body: Practices with a same-day waitlist refilled about a third of cancelled slots. With two new offices this year, empty chairs cost more to leave open.

takeaways.title: Check how it works across several offices
takeaways.body: The questions at the end cover scheduling across several offices and insurance checks. Both come up for a patient operations team running one shared desk.
